title: Sacramento Husband Charged With Wife's Murder After Claiming ICE Took Her
excerpt: Gurinder Gill told detectives immigration agents seized Jasmine Gill at her mailbox. ICE said no agents were ever there — and her burned remains had already been found in El Dorado County.
body:
• Gurinder Gill, 28, has been charged with murdering his wife Jasmine Gill, 30, whose burned remains were found in El Dorado County on October 1, the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office said.
  • Gill told detectives immigration agents had taken his wife as she checked the mail; ICE confirmed no enforcement activity took place at the home.
  • Jasmine Gill was last seen on September 30 in Sacramento's Florin area and reported missing by a cousin on October 4; the couple were in a divorce and child-custody dispute.
  • Gill was arrested on October 14, is held without bail, and was arraigned in Sacramento Superior Court on Friday. The charge is an allegation to be resolved in court.

A Sacramento man who told detectives that immigration agents had taken his wife has been charged with her murder, after her burned remains were found in the Sierra Nevada foothills. Gurinder Gill, 28, was arrested on Wednesday, October 14, on a murder warrant in the death of Jasmine Gill, 30, the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office announced on Friday.

Jasmine Gill was last seen on the evening of September 30 near Headstock Street and Allegretto Way in the Florin area of Sacramento County. Her cousin reported her missing on October 4, and sheriff's officials appealed publicly for help finding her, according to local reporting by InEDC.

The ICE claim that did not hold up

Questioned early in the investigation, Gurinder Gill claimed that US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents had taken his wife into custody while she was checking the mail outside their home. Detectives contacted ICE directly. The agency told them no enforcement activity had taken place at the residence, and investigators say they then found a series of inconsistencies in Gill's account, The Times of India reported. Detectives also learned the couple were in the middle of a divorce and a child-custody dispute.

"He was booked into the Sacramento County Main Jail, held without bail, and arraigned on Friday afternoon, according to Sacramento Superior Court records."

Remains found at a brush fire

On October 1 — a day after Jasmine Gill was last seen — crews from CAL FIRE and the US Forest Service responded to a small brush fire of about a tenth of an acre near Mormon Emigrant Trail and Bonetti Road in El Dorado County. After putting out the flames, firefighters discovered burned human remains. They were later identified as Jasmine Gill's.

Homicide detectives obtained a murder warrant, arrested Gill on October 14, and executed search warrants at two properties connected to him; the sheriff's office has not said whether evidence was recovered. He was booked into the Sacramento County Main Jail, held without bail, and arraigned on Friday afternoon, according to Sacramento Superior Court records.

Why the false ICE claim matters

The case has drawn attention in Punjab and in California's Punjabi community partly because of the cover story at its centre: a claim that federal immigration agents had seized a woman from her own mailbox, made at a moment when immigration enforcement is a live fear in immigrant households. Investigators were able to falsify it with a single call to ICE — but for four days, while a cousin's missing-person report sat open, it was the only explanation on record for where Jasmine Gill had gone.

The murder charge remains an allegation. Gill is entitled to the presumption of innocence, and the case will be resolved through the court process in Sacramento County.
